# Pandamonium v1.0.39

Open an existing Codex task with its conversation already visible, continue that same task, and inspect sources without stretching the Details card down the screen.

## MAD-876 — Workspace UI: load native task history and keep session details compact

### Problem

Selecting an existing native Codex task populated its metadata but left the chat area empty. Long attachment and activity lists expanded Details into a full-height scrolling card. Starting a continuation from a fresh catalog view also depended on an unrelated model endpoint being configured.

### Implementation

The authenticated Codex bridge now reads paginated user and assistant messages through App Server after verifying exact allowlisted project membership. The conversation opens recent turns and offers Load earlier messages. Native message IDs prevent overlap duplicates; navigation guards discard late responses. Task, workspace, model and reasoning selection survive reload, and the composer captures the intended task before sending. A native continuation can create its local conversation record without requiring a model endpoint.

Shared Details displays compact environment rows, three source previews, and short tool/output previews. View all opens a rounded, theme-aware sliding panel. It progressively loads earlier activity, retains full paths, and offers retry when a page fails. Closing or changing tasks stops further page loading. Live worker progress remains visible while Codex is still running.

### Product value and UI visibility

Choose a Codex task in Projects to read its earlier conversation and continue where it left off. Use Load earlier messages for older turns. Open Details and View all to inspect the available source, tool or output list. The shared card and panel retain the selected Pandamonium theme on desktop and phone. Assigned agent names remain configuration data.

### Verification

An authenticated running app read the actual operator task, its user/assistant messages and all 21 available sources, preserved GPT-6 Astra / Very high on reload, rejected anonymous history access with 401, and rejected a task under the wrong project with 404. A separate disposable native task completed two read-only turns through the bridge and Pandamonium composer, correctly recalled the first turn's acceptance token, and loaded the same two turns after reload. It used no tools, wrote no workspace files and was archived after verification.

Regression checks cover history order, overlapping page IDs, navigation races, retries, model/effort propagation, new-task identity retention, full source paging, theme colors, drawer focus, mobile containment, existing external-worker controls and source authorization. Full-suite and signed-artifact results are recorded in the implementation PR.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Update both Pandamonium and the selected PC Codex bridge from this release. The bridge remains the existing two-file bundle: `jarvis_codex_bridge.py` plus `atomic_io.py`. Preserve its private environment, token, workspace map, Codex home and model defaults. An older bridge cannot serve the new history endpoint; the UI reports that limitation and offers retry. Container or native app updates do not automatically replace a bridge installed on another node.

No new dependency, schema migration, Codex installation, database mirroring or additional harness is introduced. History is read from the existing native task; it is not copied into a new model prompt. Attachment names and paths are displayed; attachment binaries remain on their originating node. The integration does not replay historical tool calls or execute them while browsing. Existing external-worker task-action rules remain unchanged. The separate MCP response/recovery issue remains open.
